hero.title: The House *of Hook*
hero.lede: An NHRA member quarter-mile, built in 1957 and nicknamed for its sticky, high-traction track prep. Test-n-tune every Thursday night from March to November, plus bracket, no-prep and heads-up events.

image.alt: A blue pickup drag truck launches at night with flames from its exhaust as the crowd watches from the wall

sections.eyebrow: Why racers and fans come back
sections.title: Built *for traction*

items.title: Top-quality track prep
items.text: Sticky glue and great traction. It’s how we got our name.

items.title: Something every week
items.text: Test-n-tune, ET points series, bracket races, no-prep and grudge races and big heads-up events.

items.title: A tech department that knows racing
items.text: Our team helps make sure your vehicle is safe and ready to race.

items.title: Certified safety crew
items.text: We hope you never need them. When seconds matter, they’re there.

items.title: Two concession stands
items.text: From a cup of coffee to a full meal for the family.

items.title: Family at the track
items.text: Racer or spectator, you’re part of the family here.

items.title: Check your car
items.text: Good working order: no leaks and no loose parts or items. Bring a helmet.

items.title: Pick your tires
items.text: Run what you like, street tires included. Radials or slicks are preferred.

items.title: Get a tech card
items.text: $30, and it’s required to run. Spectators are $20; kids 12 and under get in free.

items.title: Gates at 6:30
items.text: We run until around 11 pm, March through November.

sections.title: Run by people *who race*

image.alt: An aerial view of the strip, the tower, the pits and the pine trees around the track

body: LB (Junior) Steed built Carolina Dragway in 1957. Today it’s owned by Tracy Lanning and staffed by a team who are as passionate about drag racing as the people in the lanes.

Dent Johnson has been our track announcer for more than 60 years. Behind him: track specialists Jason Hall and Chris Kneece, Henry Wyndham in the ET shack, Jeremy “Bones” Mullins in tech inspection, Paul Swygert on timing and the start, and Pete Fabisiak in staging.

items.text: Went and saw street cars on street tires not have any problems hooking. Best prepped track in SC, hands down. Family friendly, very organized, polite staff and loads of fun.
A good place to get that speed bug out of your system and be safe and have fun.
Great racing, good food, and you really have fun.

items.q: How much is it to get in on Thursday nights?
items.a: $20 for adult spectators, and kids 12 and under are free. Tech cards, required to run, are $30. Other events are priced separately.
Yes, at the gate. Uncle Bill’s Snack Shack takes cards too, but the Carolina Cafe is cash only.

items.q: Is the track open on weekends?
items.a: Only when there’s an event on the schedule.

items.q: Is it an eighth-mile or a quarter-mile?
items.a: Both. It’s a quarter-mile track with 1,800 feet of shutdown past the stripe, and it easily handles eighth-mile racing.
Yes, but no dirt bikes. Riders need a helmet, gloves, an armored jacket, jeans and high-top shoes at minimum; quicker ETs need more, up to full leathers.

items.q: Can I bring a camper or a golf cart?
items.a: Yes. Campers are $50 a weekend and golf carts $20 a weekend; a cart that comes with a race car isn’t charged.

items.q: Can I bring a chair, a grill or my dog?
items.a: Camping chairs, yes. Small grills are fine behind the fence past the bleachers, but not pull-behind or trailer grills. Small dogs are welcome on a leash at all times.
Text HOUSEOFHOOK to 84483 for instant updates on weather cancellations. There are no refunds or rain checks.

items.q: I’m new to drag racing. Where do I start?
items.a: Come to a Thursday test-n-tune with a helmet and a car in good working order. The NHRA also publishes a guide for new racers on what to expect.

sections.title: Rained out? Know first
sections.text: Text HOUSEOFHOOK to 84483 for weather-related cancellations.
